_doc: The Dawn of Man (world/dawn.js): a world begun before any town. Wandering clans settle good ground, villages grow into towns and bud new clans, towns gather villages into chiefdoms that become the realms. Years are 120 days.

barter._doc: Barter before coin (world/barter.js). A world begun at the dawn has no coin: goods are traded for goods. Coin EMERGES when barter breaks down: every checkDays the season's barter books close, and once the world's people reach popPerLand a land tile, the goods its towns bartered that season are worth tradePerLand a land tile and at least tradingShare of its towns traded (minTradingTowns at least), with the busiest town's own barter at hubTrade or more — per land tile, so a small island and a wide continent reach coin at the same stage of their growth — the first coin is struck at the busiest trading hub (the barter town with the most barter trade) from its gold and silver and its realm's (firstCoin: share of the stock above keep of target, fine = coin per unit; booked as new coin). fallbackYear: the first coin comes that year even if trade never thickens (a soft fallback). Coin then SPREADS: a barter town that traded at least spread.minValue with coin towns in a season takes up coin (up to spread.perSeason towns a season, the busiest first), its purse seeded from its own metal; and a barter town that comes to hold spread.adoptAtCoin or more in real coin (the crown's wages, a realm's payments carried in after the first coin) takes up coin too. The player deals in kind in a barter town (their purse reads the worth of the goods they carry, base prices; paying hands over goods, cheapest first and food last; being paid takes goods out of the payer's stock) and in coin in a coin town (coin is not taken in barter places). cut: the market's cut on a barter (ask = worth x (1 + cut/2), offer = worth x (1 - cut/2)). keep: a town pays in kind only from stock above this share of its target. startKit: a start purse at the dawn is given as these goods (shares of its worth). notTender: goods never handed over in payment. hintGood: the good worths are told in.

lines.noCoin: There is no coin here: offer goods.
lines.firstCoin: Barter has outgrown itself at {hub}: too many people, too many goods to weigh one against another. Its chiefs strike the first coin from their gold and silver, {coin} in all. Coin will follow the trade roads.
lines.firstCoinFallback: At {hub} the first coin is struck, {coin} in all, from the gold and silver of its stores.
lines.spread: Coin has reached {towns}: their markets now buy and sell for coin.
lines.allCoin: The last barter markets have taken up coin: the whole world buys and sells for coin now.
lines.playerCoin: Coin is used here: your coin buys, and your goods sell for coin.

eraBuildings._doc: Buildings come with the age (world/innerMap/state.js settlementLayout, by the world's current year): a building type appears in a town's plan from its year on; before it a required one is a house instead, an optional one is left out; houses of hospitality (inns, hotels) likewise. Every year here is at or before 853, so a full-grown world is laid out as it always was. A town laid out under an earlier age is laid out anew when one of these years passes.

age._doc: The world's age (world/worldAge.js): a start year from dawnYear up to matureYear gives a younger world, t = (year - dawnYear) / (matureYear - dawnYear), 0..1; matureYear and later is the full-grown world as it always was (byte for byte at the default year). A curve is at0 + (1 - at0) x t^pow. realmTowns / independents / ruins: the share of the realms' towns, the free villages and the human-made points of interest (ruins, shrines, monuments; caves and oases always stand) still standing, the oldest kept first. population: every settlement's people (a town under townMinPop becomes a village; capitals stay capitals). claim: a realm's reach about its capital (its towns keep a hex about them). roads: the longest road (hexes) laid between two towns (roadsAt0 at the dawn, no limit when mature). hinterland: the rural sites a town works. holySites: the holy sites placed. Founding years are told faster: a place founded in year Y of the full-grown world was founded dawnYear + (Y - dawnYear) x t, so nothing is founded at or after the start year, and the world's history begins at dawnYear. bands: the New Game screen's hint for a start year (upTo: t).

bands.label: a young world
bands.hint: few towns, small realms, little built — most of the land is wilderness

bands.label: a growing world
bands.hint: scattered towns, modest realms and the first roads between them

bands.label: a settled world
bands.hint: most towns founded, the realms near their full reach

bands.label: a mature world
bands.hint: the realms long founded, their towns grown and their roads laid

lines.settle: The {clan} clan made camp {where} and stayed: {name} is founded.
lines.bud: Families of {name} set out as the {clan} clan, looking for land of their own.
lines.town: {name} has grown from a village into a town.
lines.chiefdom: {ruler} of {name} gathers the villages about it: the {realm} is born.
lines.path: A trodden path now joins {a} and {b}.

welcome: The world is young. No town stands, no crown is worn. You were born to the {clan} clan, wandering the wild with your kin — {kin}. Lead them to good ground and make camp for good, and watch the first villages rise.

birth._doc: Who the player is born among at the dawn (player/dawnBirth.js): a father, a mother and siblings, all of the clan; they walk with the player while the clan does and settle in its village.

hearth._doc: Kin share their pot (DawnBirth.kinMeal): with no food in your packs, at your clan's camp or in your home village, your family feeds you — up to maxOwed meals you haven't paid back. Come home with more food than keepFood and they take it into the pot, a unit for each meal owed.

lines.fed: You eat from your family's pot: {kin} share what they have.
lines.fedOwed: Your kin feed you again, but with a look: {owed} meals now that you have not paid back. Bring food to the pot.
lines.refused: Your kin have fed you {owed} times and you have brought nothing back. Tonight there is nothing for you in the pot: hunt, forage or bring food home.
lines.repaid: You add {qty} food to your family's pot.
lines.settled: Your clan makes camp for good. {name} is your people's home now — {kin} with you.
lines.settledAway: While you were away, your clan made camp for good: {name}. Your family lives there now.
lines.settleDesc: Your clan settles here for good and founds a village: your home. Choose well — fresh water, fertile land and the shore make a village grow.
